cards.text: Here's a song from David, the shepherd who became Israel's king (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3). The heading says he wrote it when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Friend, David is in enemy hands, and he's about to talk to God about it.

cards.question: David's stuck in Gath, in Philistine hands. What's the first thing he asks God for?

cards.text: Men are hounding him, and all day they press their attack. That's like a phone that buzzes ALL DAY, and every single notification is somebody coming after you.

cards.question: True or false: David says only a few enemies are coming after him.

cards.text: Then David gets honest and says there are times he's afraid. I respect that, because I once jumped a foot in the air, gold base and all, when a kitchen timer went off.

cards.question: So when David is afraid, what does he do?

cards.text: Then David says, "In God, whose word I praise—in God I trust." And then, from the guy who JUST said he gets scared: "I will not be afraid."

cards.question: David trusts God and asks, "What can man do to me?" What's he saying about the people after him?

cards.text: But his enemies don't let up. All day long they come at David, and not even what he says is safe from them.

cards.question: All day long, David's enemies ___ his words.

cards.text: That's like telling one coworker the meeting went fine, and by lunch the whole office heard you QUIT. And it gets worse: they conspire, they lurk, and they watch David's steps.

cards.question: True or false: David says his enemies are waiting to take his life.

cards.text: Then David turns to God about all of it. He asks, "In spite of such sin, will they escape?"

cards.question: David asks God, in His anger, to ___ the nations.

cards.text: Then the song gets tender, and David talks to God about his wanderings. Not the GPS kind, where your phone says recalculating fourteen times and you STILL end up behind the same car wash.

cards.question: True or false: David says God has lost track of his wanderings.
David asks God to put his ___ in God's bottle.

cards.text: Then David asks, "…are they not in Your book?" Friend, back in the junk drawer where I spent years, the only thing anybody kept count of was the dust falling, and here's David asking God to keep his TEARS.
Then David looks ahead to a day that's coming: the day he cries for help. When I cry for help, friend, it's because my mustache got stuck in the mixer AGAIN.

cards.question: On the day David cries for help, what will his enemies do?
True or false: David says he will know that God is on his side.

cards.text: Then here comes that line again, and this time "In God, whose word I praise" gets a partner: "in the LORD, whose word I praise." And once more, David trusts in God and will not be afraid.
Then David tells God he's bound by his vows to Him, and he's ready to follow through. That's more than I can say for the promise I make every morning to hit snooze only once.

cards.question: David's ready to follow through on his vows. What will he give God?
David gives thanks because God delivered his soul from ___.
God delivered David's soul from death and his feet from stumbling. David says it's so he can do what?

answers.text: Walk before God in the light of life
Rest in God's house for the length of days
Stand among his people in the city gate
